subject: research/accel-lutft
professional: a reviewer for an ML-hardware co-design venue (MLSys, DATE, ISLPED or IEEE TCAD) who works on weight-sharing / lookup-table inference accelerators. They would check first that the energy model and the accuracy model describe the same arithmetic (activation and codebook widths), that the trained-quantisation baseline follows Deep Compression's recipe or explains why not, that the 'fine-tuning helps' claims survive paired uncertainty, and that LUT-inference prior work (Deep Compression's codebook fine-tuning, UNPU, LUT-GEMM style product tables) is positioned against

evidence.correctness: Every reported number reproduces and three kinds of output recompute against code I wrote. `python3 experiments/run.py` in a scratch copy (66 s) gives results.json and results.txt byte-identical to the committed files. Energies recomputed by hand from the stated model (my own script, no import of the subject) match every energy cell: int8 dense 3.559 nJ, int8 pruned 1.507, K=2/4/8 dense @0.04 2.302/2.830/3.506, pruned 1.304/1.547/1.939, @0.16 7.218/8.114/9.527 and 2.809/3.421/4.550. Means, paired drops and standard errors recomputed from results.json with the statistics module match all 14 rows. For seed 0 my own forward pass (8-bit max-calibrated activations) reproduces float32 0.9753 and post2/4/8 0.4423/0.8984/0.9533 (dense) and 0.9396/0.9698/0.9670 (pruned) exactly. Not 4: the codebook is a Lloyd local optimum, not the k-means optimum: an exact 1-D k-means by dynamic programming gives up to 18% lower SSE (K=8 pruned seed 0: 8.31 vs 9.83) and moves single-seed accuracy by up to 1.1 points (dense K=4: 0.887 exact, 0.898 Lloyd, 0.885 sklearn), the same size as the fine-tuning effects reported at K=4 and 8.
evidence.completeness: README promises: 4 tests in under 1 s (Ran 4 tests in 0.097s OK); run.py about 2 min (66 s, byte-identical outputs); --report rebuilds results.txt (run.py ends with report(), identical); figure.py writes experiments/frontier.png (FAILS: figure.py:1-32 now writes lutft.svg, a different plot of accuracy against K; frontier.png is a stale committed file no script in the tree regenerates). Results table matches results.txt in every cell. Post-training rows reproduce accel-lut's results.txt (share2/4/8 accuracies, drops and energies identical) as claimed. Not-done list (RTL, real KWS data, recipe sweep, centroid-gradient scheme) is honest.
evidence.verification: Tests pass (4 OK). Five seeded mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py, 1 caught (codebook size K -> K+1, lut.py:23), 4 survived: dropping the table-read term from the per-weight LUT energy (lut.py:55, which changes every table-engine energy and the 14% headline); removing the mask from the straight-through gradient (model.py:88); int8 weight width 8 -> 4 in the baseline energy (run.py:76); and evaluating the un-fine-tuned params in the ft rows (run.py:65, which would erase the project's whole effect). test_energy_matches_lut_model (tests/test_lutft.py:37) compares run.energy to the same lut.energy_lut_pj it calls, so it can never fail on a wrong constant; no test pins a hand-computed energy or results.txt.
evidence.craft: Read src/accel_lutft/lut.py (56 lines), model.py (121), experiments/run.py (103), figure.py (91), tests/test_lutft.py (40). Small and readable, but: model.py and lut.py are copied from accel-lut (itself copied from accel-sparse), a third copy of the engine (README.md:7 says so); figure.py carries its own ~60-line SVG plotter instead of research/_shared/linefig.py, as research/CLAUDE.md asks; the x axis of lutft.svg is labelled 'table weight width (bits)' while it plots K = 2, 4, 8 codebook entries (1, 2, 3 index bits) (figure.py:31-32); `int(n.lstrip('postft'))` parses design names by stripping a character set (run.py:78); the k-means codebook is re-fit with 5 Lloyd iterations on every minibatch, an O(n*K) per step cost that a fixed-assignment scheme avoids.
evidence.claims: Checked: 'cuts the drop from 6.5 to 1.7 points' (backed, results.txt), '14% under int8' (1.30/1.51 = 0.861, backed), 'se 0.4 points' (backed), '0.2 nJ margin' (1.51-1.30, backed), 'at 0.16 pJ/bit the table loses everywhere' (backed, 2.81+ vs 1.51, 7.22+ vs 3.56), 'fine-tuned K=8 is worse 3.2 vs 1.6 points' (backed; paired ft8-post8 = -1.6 points, 0 wins 10 losses). Not backed: the headline 'Fine-tuning rescues K = 2 and 4 in the 75%-pruned network' (README.md:3): pruned K=4 was already within 2 points without fine-tuning (drop 1.6) and fine-tuning moved it +0.08 points (paired se 0.35, 4 wins 4 losses); only K=2 is rescued (+4.7 points, 10/10 wins), as research/README.md:339 itself says. The Figure paragraph (README.md:52) and Reproduce line (README.md:22) describe frontier.png, which figure.py no longer writes. Deep Compression citation flagged as unverified, energy constants disclosed as assumptions, AI assistance disclosed.
evidence.fitness: A researcher can rerun it in a minute and extend it, and the README frames it honestly as a hypothesis. But it does not reach the research/CLAUDE.md bar (programme aimed at a venue): one 64-32-10 MLP on 8x8 digits, one fine-tuning recipe with no validation sweep, and the result that trained shared values recover low-K accuracy is the expected one since Han, Mao and Dally (2016), who report 2-4-bit shared FC weights near lossless after centroid fine-tuning. The project's own recipe is worse than no fine-tuning at dense K=8 in 10 of 10 splits, which points at the recipe rather than the question. LUT-inference hardware work (UNPU, Lee et al. 2018 JSSC; LUT-GEMM, Park et al. 2024) is not cited, so the energy claim is not positioned.
evidence.domain: Against Deep Compression's trained quantisation (fixed cluster assignments, gradients accumulated into centroids) the method departs knowingly (straight-through to latent weights with the codebook re-fit each step) and says so. Departures a reviewer would flag: the energy model charges first-layer activations at 4 bits (run.py:12 ABITS=[4,8]) while the accuracy model feeds unquantised inputs with 17 levels (0..16/16, 5 bits); codebook values stay float in accuracy but are costed as 8-bit multiplier operands and 16-bit table entries (lut.py:52-55) with no check that 16-bit products suffice; the k-means codebook is a Lloyd local optimum whose initialisation noise (~1 point) is as large as the K=4/8 effects; no learning-rate or epoch sweep; table-read energy (the decisive parameter) is swept at only two points, not to the crossover.

defects.what: Energy model and experiment harness are untested: dropping the table-read term from the LUT energy, changing the int8 weight width, or reporting the un-fine-tuned model in the ft rows all leave every test green; test_energy_matches_lut_model compares run.energy with the same lut function it calls, so it cannot fail on a wrong constant.

Headline says fine-tuning 'rescues K = 2 and 4' in the pruned network; at K=4 the post-training design was already within 2 points and fine-tuning changed accuracy by +0.08 points (paired se 0.35, 4 wins 4 losses). Only K=2 is rescued (research/README.md:339 says so correctly).

README says figure.py writes experiments/frontier.png (accuracy vs energy); figure.py now writes lutft.svg (accuracy vs K), so the committed frontier.png cannot be regenerated, and lutft.svg labels K = 2, 4, 8 codebook entries as 'table weight width (bits)'.

Energy charges 4-bit first-layer activations while the accuracy model feeds unquantised 17-level inputs (5 bits), and codebook values are float in the accuracy model but costed as 8-bit operands and 16-bit products.

Lloyd k-means from quantile init is a local optimum (up to 18% above the exact 1-D optimum in SSE); quantiser noise moves single-seed accuracy by ~1 point, the size of the K=4/8 fine-tuning effects being interpreted.

Result that trained shared values recover low-K accuracy is expected from Deep Compression (2016); LUT-inference hardware prior work (UNPU 2018, LUT-GEMM 2024) not cited; single recipe, no sweep, toy task: below the research/CLAUDE.md programme bar.
model.py and lut.py are a third copy of the accel-sparse/accel-lut engine; figure.py carries its own SVG plotter instead of research/_shared/linefig.py.

verdict: A small, honest, fully reproducible follow-up: run.py regenerates results.json and results.txt byte-identically in 66 s, every energy cell matches hand arithmetic, every mean and paired se matches an independent recomputation, and my own forward pass reproduces the seed-0 post-training accuracies exactly. It misses the bar on claims, verification and the research bar. The headline 'rescues K = 2 and 4' overstates the data (K=4 moved +0.08 points, within noise, and was already inside the tolerance); the README's figure no longer matches figure.py; four of five seeded mutants, including one that reports the un-fine-tuned model as fine-tuned, survive the tests. The finding is the one Deep Compression predicts, on an 8x8-digits MLP with one recipe that hurts dense K=8 in 10 of 10 splits, and the energy and accuracy models disagree on input width. Median 2.
